title: Adaptive Signal Prioritizer for Canary Aborts
creator: Marco Nguyen
description: Design and implement a classifier-like prioritizer that composes heterogeneous SLO signals (latency p95, error rate, token cost per response, throughput) into a single, interpretable abort score for canary rollouts. The prioritizer must support cohort-aware weighting, lightweight online tuning, and a small grace/hysteresis window to avoid noisy false positives.
background_and_context: Current canary decisioning in Redwood is a rule-based evaluation of individual metrics with fixed thresholds per rollout. This causes brittle abort decisions when signals disagree (e.g., slight latency increase but large cost regression) and requires manual threshold tuning per model/route. Teams have spent cycles tuning thresholds for each product and we lack a standardized, auditable mechanism for combining signals into a single abort decision score that can be tuned automatically and rolled out across teams.
proposed_solution: Introduce an 'Adaptive Signal Prioritizer' service component that ingests per-route per-cohort metric streams and produces a continuous abort_score in [0,1]. The algorithm will: 1) normalize heterogeneous signals using historical baselines and robust statistics (median+MAD), 2) convert normalized deltas into per-signal risk contributions via sigmoid transforms with configurable steepness, 3) compute a weighted sum where weights are cohort- and route-specific and can be updated via a lightweight Bayesian posterior update using labeled past rollouts, and 4) apply temporal smoothing (exponential moving average) plus a grace window to enforce hysteresis. Admins can set policy-level thresholds on abort_score (e.g., abort if >0.7 for >= 3 minutes) and tune cost vs latency weighting per org. The prioritizer will export the breakdown (per-signal contributions) for observability and audit.
design_notes:
- Normalization: use rolling baseline of 7 days with percentile bucketing to handle seasonality.
- Sigmoid mapping anchors at delta=0 and saturates at large regressions to prevent domination by Outliers.
- Bayesian weight priors seeded from product defaults; update when labelled outcomes (abort confirmed good vs false alarm) are available.
- Grace window: configurable minutes and optional cohort quorum (e.g., require signal across 2+ cohorts).
- Provide a 'safe mode' fallback that maps prioritizer outputs back to existing rule-based thresholds for compatibility.
- Telemetry: tokenized per-request attribution sample for privacy and cost constraints.
implementation_plan: 1) Build a lightweight prioritizer library (Go) with pluggable normalization and mapping functions. 2) Instrument runtime to emit per-route metric vectors in the expected format. 3) Implement an orchestrator to aggregate cohort streams and compute abort_score. 4) Add console UI card showing abort_score + contributions and a toggle to enable prioritizer in canary policies. 5) Run shadow experiment for 2 weeks, compare abort decisions vs baseline rules, tune priors. 6) Gradual opt-in rollout to 10% of teams, then broader rollout with retroactive audits.
acceptance_criteria: Prioritizer library with unit tests for normalization and mapping functions merged to monorepo
Abort_score exported to the console and stored in rollout traces for every canary run in shadow mode
Shadow run shows >= 20% reduction in false-positive aborts on historical testbeds while preserving true-positive aborts (within 5%)
Admins can configure policy-level abort threshold and grace window from Console
Fallback mode reproduces existing rule-based decisions when enabled
Documentation and runbook for troubleshooting and manual override are published
metrics_and_success_criteria: - Reduction in manual threshold adjustments by SRE/PM teams (tracked via support tickets). - False-positive abort rate drop on synthetic historical rollouts >= 20%. - Time-to-detect real regressions unchanged or improved (within 10%). - Observability: 100% of canary traces include per-signal contribution breakdown. - Customer impact risk classified as 'medium' and validated in pre-rollout review.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for normalization, sigmoid mapping, and smoothing. - Integration tests against rollout simulator that replays production metric streams. - Offline evaluation: run prioritizer on last 6 months of rollout traces and compute confusion matrix against known abort outcomes. - Shadow deployment: enable prioritizer in watch-only mode for 2 weeks across multiple routes and compare decisions. - Canary rollout: enable on a single low-risk model with manual abort override available.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal dev testing and library stabilization. Phase 1: shadow across three product routes (2 weeks). Phase 2: opt-in pilot (10% orgs, 4 weeks) with weekly tuning. Phase 3: org-wide opt-in with policy templates and training. Provide opt-out path and safe-mode for 30 days post-rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overfitting weights to historical rollouts leading to missed real regressions. Mitigation: conservative priors, minimum weight floor for safety-relevant signals (error rate & latency). Risk: added complexity and alert fatigue. Mitigation: expose transparent per-signal contributions and default conservative thresholds. Risk: privacy/cost from per-request attribution. Mitigation: sample attribution at 0.1% and aggregate at cohort level.
notes: This ticket prioritizes interpretability: every abort_score must be accompanied by a per-signal breakdown so operators can quickly understand root cause and override if needed. The approach aims to reduce toil for teams that currently maintain per-route threshold spreadsheets.
follow_up_tasks: Train on-call SREs on interpretability dashboard
Set up periodic weight-review job to detect drift
